svg.title: op-reason's SSH relay: the window, the toasts and the notifications
svg.desc: Animation of a Windows desktop. A signature that passes without a window shows a small light yellow card, a toast, at the top left, at 90% opacity so that the text behind shows through faintly: Passed · Human, the ssh command and its destination, allowed for this terminal · no reason given; it fades after four seconds. An ansible run signs eight times in one call: one card counts them (×2 … ×8), shows the last host and lights up at each. Three other calls each put a card on top and push the others down; a fourth and a fifth push the oldest out at once, and +N under the third card counts the cards pushed out (+1, +2) until four seconds after their last signature; four seconds after its last signature each card fades. Then a new call asks in op-reason's window at the top right, with its Windows notification at the bottom right, while another toast comes at the top left; a click on Allow this call closes the window and its notification together, and the call's later signatures come as one toast at the top left (×3).
